name: 20452-repeatimage-ayavision32b-4gpu
hardware: 4x H100 80GB HBM3, four GPUs of one a3 node (--gres=gpu:4).
parallelism: TP=4, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=32, bounded at 512 requests with an 1800 s safety cap, warmup the first 20% by completion. safety_seconds 1800 is a runaway guard rather than a bound.
workload: Real visual question answering from `merve/vqav2-small` (split `validation`), one photograph and one short question per request, output pinned to 64 tokens (`max_tokens` = `min_tokens` = 64). The guidellm `huggingface` split expression concatenates the same 64-row slice eight times, so the run is 512 requests over 64 distinct images in order, eight passes. Driven in-process through guidellm's `vllm_python` backend, so no HTTP hop is timed.
purpose: A visual question answering service on a 32-billion-parameter vision model, answering photo questions for 32 concurrent users across four GPUs.
launch:
# Flags for the pinned engine, v0.10.2rc2-19-g9f04d9d55f (2025-09-12). These become
# `AsyncEngineArgs` fields: a key this build does not define fails at engine construction.

model: unsloth/aya-vision-32b

tensor-parallel-size: 4

# Well above the measured worst case, 2322 prompt tokens for a 4:3 photograph plus its question,
# and at this checkpoint's ceiling: aya-vision-32b declares max_position_embeddings=8192, and
# the engine REFUSES a larger value ("User-specified max_model_len (16384) is greater than the
# derived max_model_len") rather than clamping it. At 16384 no engine is constructed and all
# 512 requests error.
max-model-len: 8192

# Equal to the declared stream count, so the scheduler admits the whole in-flight set.
max-num-seqs: 32

# The executor backend, pinned rather than inferred. vLLM picks "ray" on its own whenever
# `cuda_device_count_stateless() < world_size` (config/parallel.py:383-390). That happened on
# 2026-08-21: a worker that exported CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 left one visible device against
# world_size 4, the backend flipped to "ray", and the run spent 1800 s in `_wait_until_pg_ready`
# before dying. All four GPUs must be visible to the process; this key keeps the backend
# independent of any stray export. It matches the source, whose
# `vllm serve --tensor-parallel-size 4` on a single node also resolves to "mp".
distributed-executor-backend: mp
